The PR description also states: "`scripts/review_rb_judge.sh` and `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` already refuse to call `gh pr merge` without `--match-head-commit`".
  Expected change site: `scripts/review_rb_judge.sh` lines 1720-1721 (judge `merge` action branch) and lines 1749-1750 (judge terminal-`fix`-treated-as-merge branch), both inside the case `merge)` and case `fix)` IS_FINAL fallthrough respectively, which are also reached via `bash "${SUPPORT_SCRIPTS_DIR}/review_rb_judge.sh"` invoked from `review_autofix.yml:5735`.
  Evidence of absence: LAST RUN DIFF and full PR DIFF do not modify `scripts/review_rb_judge.sh` at all (the changed-files list is `review_autofix.yml`, `changelog.d/4109-bind-auto-merge-to-evaluated-head.md`, `scripts/review_enable_auto_merge.sh`, `tests/test_review_autofix_review_pipeline_contract.py`). Direct read of the file confirms the four calls at lines 1720-1721 and 1749-1750 use `gh pr merge "${PR_NUMBER}" --repo "${REPOSITORY}" --squash --auto` with no `--match-head-commit` flag, while the sibling `merge_with_followup` branch at line 2179-2180 already constructs `_match_head_arg=(--match-head-commit "${PR_HEAD_SHA}")` and applies it.
  Why it fails at runtime: A push landing between the judge's mergeability poll (which captures `PR_HEAD_SHA` for `merge_with_followup`) and the merge call in the `merge` or terminal-`fix` branch will be merged by GitHub even though the judge never evaluated the new head.
- Requirement: "Every `gh pr merge` on the review_autofix path is bound to the head SHA that was actually evaluated (`--match-head-commit`)".
  Expected change site: `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` `merge_with_followup` action only (around line 19330) currently passes `--match-head-commit`; the other poller merge paths (lines 14928-14929 wave-merge auto-merge, 17351-17352 wave-merge squash, 18046/18049 review-blocked batch squash path, 18836/18839 and 18893-18894 review-blocked merge calls, 19184-19185 review-blocked merge, 21786 noop-suspicious force-merge).

  Why it fails at runtime: Any orchestrator-managed PR that reaches one of the unbound poller merge paths can be merged over a head the orchestrator never observed.
